newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Chairman Allen in successful surgery.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Chairman Allen in successful surgery.

text.p: Robert Allen, chairman of AT&T Corp, underwent successful heart surgery earlier in the day at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minn., the company said Thursday.
Allen, 62, was resting "comfortably" following surgery to replace his aortic valve, correcting a congenital condition, it said.
"The surgery was entirely elective and had been scheduled for several months," it said. "His doctors do not anticipate he will have any physical restrictions."
The company said Allen had known about his condition "for decades" and decided to undergo surgery after a recent physical examination showed a slight constriction of his aortic valve.

"While that is normal in such conditions, Allen decided to have the problem corrected before any symptoms developed," it said, adding that the chairman planned to return to work by the end of the month.
AT&T said Allen had talked to the board about the decision in December. In his absence chief operating officer and CEO-designate John Walter was in charge of the company, a spokesman said.

Wall Street has been very sensitive to AT&T management changes in recent months, and particularly the succession to Allen, but took this one in its stride. The shares remained 3/8 weaker at 1530 EST/2030 GMT. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
